claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr is a single-phase BCC solid solution.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a yield strength of approximately 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
Replacing half of the Hf fraction with V to form Hf0.5V0.5MoTaTiZr will reduce density by approximately 5–10%.
Hf0.5V0.5MoTaTiZr will retain approximately the room-temperature mechanical performance of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Hf0.5V0.5MoTaTiZr will retain approximately the high-temperature yield strength of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The modified Hf0.5V0.5MoTaTiZr alloy will retain a single-phase BCC solid solution.
Vanadium substitution will induce lattice distortion in the modified alloy.
V-induced lattice distortion will contribute to solid-solution strengthening after partial replacement of Hf.
Replacing Hf with lower-atomic-mass V lowers the alloy's overall density.
Vanadium will stabilize the BCC matrix.
Matrix stabilization and lattice-distortion strengthening will maintain high yield strength at room temperature and 1000 °C.
The modified alloy will have a room-temperature yield strength near 1600 MPa under quasi-static loading.
The modified alloy will have a yield strength of 800–855 MPa at 1000 °C under quasi-static loading.
The modified alloy's ductility and fracture toughness will remain within 90–100% of the as-cast baseline.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires both ductility and fracture toughness to remain within 90–100% of baseline, but the rejection rule explicitly applies the 10% degradation threshold only to ductility and does not state that an excessive fracture-toughness loss independently rejects the hypothesis.
